summary: The prepared main source already contains the reporter-confirmed fix from upstream PR #32954 / merge commit 166c6f71811087d427feed48c685356965810707: a trailing cluster arrive/wait barrier gated to the two-CTA TGV kernel. No additional production change was justified; a structural regression was added.

tests.what_was_measured: Three structural checks passed: the checked-in kernel has the gated trailing barrier, a missing wait is rejected, and a barrier before dispatch is rejected.
Failing-before evidence on exact release commit 29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102: AssertionError: missing two-CTA cluster arrive/wait exit barrier.

A float32 32x64 by 64x16 GEMM ran on AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 and matched a CPU float64-derived reference with max absolute error 2.1457672119140625e-06. This does not exercise the NVIDIA-only affected kernel.

gpu_execution_evidence: Real execution used the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-0c4ad14625fe/evidence/gfx950-runtime.txt. The issue-specific SM103 kernel was not executable on this GPU.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA SM10x/SM103 GPU was available, so the CuTe DSL TGV kernel and its emitted CUDA ISA were not compiled or executed locally.
Kimi-K3 and RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark weights were unavailable; no full serving or semantic-accuracy reproduction was performed.
The reported TP8 workload cannot be reproduced on the assigned single GPU.

The original low-probability PDL/CUDA-graph scheduling race is not deterministic in a small fixture; issue resolution relies on the accepted root-cause evidence, production A/B in PR #32954, and the reporter's confirmation.
